paper_title: SepLLM Accelerate Large Language Models by Compressing One Segment into   One Separator
caption: Training loss curves for the post-training setting.
model_annotation: The plot illustrates the training loss curves for different configurations of SepLLM and a vanilla model during post-training, with loss on the y-axis and the number of iterations on the x-axis. The x-axis is labeled “#Iteration” and spans from approximately 95,000 to 125,000, using a linear scale with tick marks every 5,000 iterations. The y-axis is labeled “Loss” and ranges from 2.0 to 3.0, also on a linear scale, with tick marks every 0.2 units. Four distinct lines are shown: a magenta solid line with markers for “SepLLM (n=64, larger lr)”, a blue solid line with markers for “SepLLM (n=128)”, an orange solid line with markers for “SepLLM (n=64)”, and a red dashed line for “Vanilla before post-training”. The magenta line starts at a loss of about 3.0 at 95,000 iterations and decreases steadily to approximately 2.2 by 125,000 iterations. The blue line begins slightly below 3.0 and declines to around 2.3 by the end. The orange line starts near 3.0 and converges to about 2.3 as well. The red dashed line remains constant at a loss of 2.4 across all iterations, serving as a baseline. All three SepLLM curves show a consistent downward trend, indicating decreasing loss with increasing iterations, while the vanilla model’s loss remains unchanged.
